title: Volume conversions: L and mL
blurb: Convert between litres and millilitres in both directions, add mixed volumes safely and type the answer in the unit the box asks for.
question: A client's daily drink target is 1.5 L. By mid-afternoon they have had 250 mL, 300 mL and 0.4 L. How many more millilitres do they need?

teach.body: The litre (L) and millilitre (mL) are linked by one factor: 1 L = 1000 mL, and 1 mL = 0.001 L. Plain English: a litre jug holds a thousand millilitre spoonfuls. Litres to millilitres, multiply by 1000; millilitres to litres, divide by 1000. Bags, jugs and fluid targets are often in litres; syringes, pots, feeds and fluid charts are in millilitres.

head: Litres
Millilitres
teach.caption: Write the unit as mL, with a capital L, and never add an s.

teach.body: Before adding volumes, put them all in the same unit, usually mL. 0.4 L + 250 mL is not 250.4 of anything: convert first (400 mL + 250 mL = 650 mL). Convert to litres at the end if the question asks for L.

teach.h: Worked example: a supported living home
items: Rhys, a client with a learning disability, has a drink target of 1.5 L a day. His support nurse, Megan Hughes, checks his chart at 1500.
Convert the target: 1.5 L x 1000 = 1500 mL.
Add his drinks in mL: 250 + 300 + 400 (0.4 L) = 950 mL.
Sense check: he has had just under 1 L of a 1.5 L target, so just over half a litre is left.

teach.text: 1.75 L is not 1 L and 75 mL: the digits after the point are fractions of a litre, so 0.75 L = 750 mL and 1.75 L = 1750 mL. And always check which unit the answer box shows: 1.5 L typed into a box marked mL must be 1500.

items: L to mL: x 1000. mL to L: ÷ 1000.
Convert everything to one unit before adding or subtracting.
Digits after the point are fractions of a litre: 0.75 L = 750 mL.
Type the number in the unit the box shows, with no commas.

summary: You can now convert between litres and millilitres in both directions, total volumes given in mixed units, and check that your answer fits the unit printed by the answer box.

A.q: Convert 850 mL to litres. Please use the correct unit and write your answer to two decimal places.
A.why: mL to L: ÷ 1000. 850 ÷ 1000 = 0.85 L. Sense check: under 1000 mL is under 1 L.

whyNot.0: Divided by 100; mL to L is ÷ 1000.
whyNot.1: Divided by 10000; mL to L is ÷ 1000.
whyNot.2: Divided by 10; mL to L is ÷ 1000.

whyNot.0: Multiplied by 100; L to mL is x 1000.
whyNot.2: Read 1.75 L as 1 L and 75 mL; 0.75 L is 750 mL.
whyNot.3: Multiplied by 10000; L to mL is x 1000.

B.q: In a residential home, a client drinks 250 mL, 180 mL, 320 mL and 150 mL over a morning. What is the total in litres? Please use the correct unit and write your answer to one decimal place.

whyNot.0: Divided 900 by 100; mL to L is ÷ 1000.
whyNot.1: Divided 900 by 10000; mL to L is ÷ 1000.
whyNot.2: Divided 900 by 10; mL to L is ÷ 1000.

B.q: A person taking lithium on a mental health ward is encouraged to drink 2.5 L a day. By 1600 they have drunk 1650 mL. How many more millilitres do they need to drink?
B.why: 2.5 L = 2500 mL. 2500 - 1650 = 850 mL still to drink.

whyNot.1: Read 2.5 L as 2050 mL; 2.5 L is 2500 mL.
whyNot.2: Moved the point two places left; 2500 - 1650 is 850.

B.q: A 0.5 L bag of fluid is hung and 175 mL has been infused. How many millilitres remain in the bag?

whyNot.0: Used 1000 mL as the bag volume; 0.5 L is 500 mL.
whyNot.1: Dropped a place in the subtraction.
whyNot.3: Dropped two places in the subtraction.

C.q: A client is prescribed lactulose 15 mL twice a day. A full bottle holds 0.5 L. How many complete days will one bottle last? Write your answer as a whole number.
C.why: 0.5 L = 500 mL. Each day uses 15 x 2 = 30 mL. 500 ÷ 30 = 16.7, so 16 complete days.

whyNot.0: Rounded 16.7 up; only 16 complete days are covered.
whyNot.1: This is the number of 15 mL doses, not days.
whyNot.3: Treated 0.5 L as 50 mL; 0.5 L is 500 mL.

C.q: A client with a learning disability receives 1.2 L of feed through a PEG over 24 hours, plus six water flushes of 50 mL. What is the total volume in litres? Please use the correct unit and write your answer to one decimal place.
C.why: Flushes: 6 x 50 = 300 mL. Feed: 1.2 L = 1200 mL. Total 1500 mL = 1.5 L.

whyNot.1: Counted one flush; there are six (300 mL).
whyNot.2: Treated each 50 mL flush as 0.5 L.
whyNot.3: Divided 1500 mL by 100; mL to L is ÷ 1000.

C.q: On a mental health ward, a person drinks 0.35 L, 0.2 L and 425 mL. What is the total in millilitres?

whyNot.0: Converted 0.2 L to 20 mL; 0.2 L is 200 mL.
whyNot.1: Converted 0.35 L to 35 mL and 0.2 L to 20 mL.
whyNot.2: Added litres and millilitres without converting.

reteach.title: Think in jugs and spoonfuls
reteach.question: How many 1 mL spoonfuls would fill a litre jug?

blocks.body: A litre is a big unit and a millilitre a tiny one: 1000 mL fill 1 L. So turning litres into millilitres always makes the number bigger (x 1000), and turning millilitres into litres makes it smaller (÷ 1000).

blocks.text: Add volumes only once they share a unit; 0.2 L + 425 mL is 625 mL, not 425.2.

explain.body: 0.05 L is five hundredths of a litre: 0.05 x 1000 = 50 mL.

test.q: How many millilitres are in 0.05 L?

whyNot.0: Multiplied by 100; L to mL is x 1000.
whyNot.2: That is 0.5 L; 0.05 L is ten times less.
whyNot.3: Multiplied by 10; L to mL is x 1000.
